subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Mercury: The Swift Planet
description: A quick win: understand Mercury: The Swift Planet.

hook.text: Mercury orbits the Sun in 88 days but rotates so slowly that one day lasts 59 Earth days.

buildup.text: It's the smallest planet—barely larger than our Moon. Its battered surface is covered in craters.

discovery.text: Temperatures swing from 430°C by day to −180°C at night. No atmosphere means no heat retention.

twist.text: Despite being closest to the Sun, Mercury is not the hottest planet. Venus holds that record.

climax.text: NASA's MESSENGER found ice in permanently shadowed craters near Mercury's poles.

punchline.text: Closest to the Sun, yet hiding ice in its shadows.

quiz.question: Why isn't Mercury the hottest planet despite being closest to the Sun?
options: It has no atmosphere to trap heat, while Venus has a thick heat-trapping atmosphere
Mercury reflects most sunlight back into space
It spins too fast for heat to build up

details.summary: Mercury is the smallest planet and closest to the Sun, orbiting in just 88 days at temperatures ranging from 430°C in sunlight to -180°C at night. Despite its heat, ice exists in permanently shadowed craters at its poles.
details.whyItMatters: Mercury challenges planet formation models — why is its iron core so large relative to its mantle? It may have lost its outer layers in a giant impact or through solar evaporation.
takeaways: Mercury orbits the Sun in just 88 days with extreme temperatures
Ice exists in permanently shadowed polar craters despite the heat
Its iron core is unusually massive at 85% of its radius

faq.question: How can ice exist on Mercury?
faq.answer: Mercury has almost no axial tilt, so deep craters near the poles have floors that never see sunlight — permanently shadowed regions where temperatures stay below -170°C. Water ice delivered by comets and asteroids accumulates in these frozen traps, confirmed by radar and the MESSENGER spacecraft.

faq.question: Has any spacecraft visited Mercury?
faq.answer: Mariner 10 flew past three times in 1974-75, mapping 45% of the surface. MESSENGER orbited Mercury from 2011-2015, mapping the entire surface and discovering polar ice. The ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission, launched in 2018, is en route and will arrive in orbit in 2025.
